narrative.coaching_note: The most important change next time in this situation is to wash your hands with soap and water after touching bed rail A and before touching resident A. You touched bed rail A with your bare hand starting at 1.6 seconds, and those germs stayed on your bare hand. You then touched phone starting at 8.1 seconds, which moved contamination from bed rail A to phone. You then touched resident A starting at 21.4 seconds, which carried contamination to resident A. Because this was C. difficile, alcohol rub does not kill the spores, so use soap and water and rub for the full 40 seconds. Cleaning your hands at that point would have kept bare hand, gloved hand, phone and resident A clean.
narrative.audit_summary: Source was bed rail A. Bare hand contacted bed rail A at 1.6 seconds, call button at 7.6 seconds, phone at 8.1 and 12.4 seconds, and resident A at 21.4 seconds, producing transfers from bed rail A to bare hand, then to call button, phone, and resident A at 21.4 seconds with 1 resident exposure. Hand hygiene compliance was 0 of 2 opportunities: Moment 1 was 0 of 1 and Moment 5 was 0 of 1; Moments 2 and 4 had no opportunities. No hygiene events occurred; for C. difficile, soap and water is required because alcohol rub does not kill spores. No glove use issue was noted. Disinfect phone, bed rail A, call button, and resident A zone. Use an EPA List K sporicidal disinfectant (effective against C. difficile spores); standard disinfectants do not kill spores.
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene with soap and water at 8.1 seconds.
